s.c: In a number of languages the use of ἀναγεννάω in the sense of ‘to be born again spiritually’ is extremely difficult for people to understand, even as it was in biblical times. However, the concept is such an integral element in so much NT thought and teaching that the expression should be retained, though it may very well require some brief marginal explanation or at least significant cross-referencing.|In its NT usage ἀναγεννάω, of course, has nothing to do with birth as such, but refers to a radical change in personality, with the attendant change in state, and it is for that reason that ἀναγεννάω is here classified in Domain 13 Be, Become, Exist, Happen. s.c: In some instances ἀναγκάζω and δέω may be rendered as ‘to cause it to be necessary for.’ In other instances a simple causative seems to be the closest equivalent. For example, the last clause of ⟦Galatians 2:14|Galatians 2:14⟧ may be expressed as ‘how can you make Gentiles live like Jews,’ and in ⟦Acts 20:22|Acts 20:22⟧ one may translate ‘and now the Spirit makes me go to Jerusalem.’

In the various contexts of the book of Acts it is preferable to use a term which implies a harbor, while in contexts which speak of the Sea of Galilee, movement would normally be from a beach (see LN 54.5).

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to come back to life after having once died
s.g: to come back to life; to live again; to be resurrected; resurrection
s.c: This word is also found as a variant reading: Χριστὸς καὶ ἀπέθανεν καὶ ἀνέστη καὶ ἀνέζησεν ‘Christ also died, rose, and lives again’ ⟦Romans 14:9|Romans 14:9⟧ (apparatus).|In a number of languages there is a difficulty involved in formulating some expression for ‘resurrection’ or ‘living again,’ since such a phrase may refer to what is technically known as metempsychosis, that is to say, the rebirth of the soul in another existence, a belief which is widely held in a number of areas of south Asia. This problem may be avoided in some languages by speaking of ‘his body will live again’ or ‘his body will come back to life’ or ‘he will be the same person when he lives again.’|In ⟦Luke 15:24|Luke 15:24⟧, ὅτι οὗτος ὁ υἱός μου νεκρὸς ἦν καὶ ἀνέζησεν ‘because this son of mine was dead and he has come back to life,’ the figurative hyperbole may reflect the practice of referring to a person as dead and then coming back to life if he has been completely separated for a time from all family relations, but then has later been discovered alive and well. It is possible, of course, that in ⟦Luke 15:24|Luke 15:24⟧ the expression is an idiom, but it is more likely to be simply a figurative usage.

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἀναζάω<SDBG:ἀναζάω:000000>}[a] ‘to come back to life,’ {D:23.93}) to begin to function, with a possible implication of the suddenness of the action{N:001}

s.g: to reactivate; to cause to begin to be active again
s.c: It may also be possible to translate ἀναζωπυρέω in ⟦2 Timothy 1:6|2 Timothy 1:6⟧ as ‘to cause to take on new life.’ A few translators have used an expression such as ‘to keep alive the gift,’ primarily in order to avoid the impression that Timothy had in some measure departed from his earlier dedication to the gospel.

s.c: It is also possible to translate ἀνάθεμα in ⟦Romans 9:3|Romans 9:3⟧ as ‘I would wish that God himself had cursed me.’

s.d: to invoke divine harm if what is said is not true or if one does not carry out what has been promised{N:001}

s.c: In ⟦Mark 14:71|Mark 14:71⟧ ἀναθεματίζω is in many regards similar in meaning to ὄμνυμι (LN 33.463), but ἀναθεματίζω specifically denotes a curse which was invoked by Peter if what he was saying was not true.

s.d: to observe closely and give serious consideration to, suggesting the possibility of something unusual

s.c: In ⟦Acts 17:23|Acts 17:23⟧ ἀναθεωρέω implies considerable mental activity, for Paul was not merely looking at the objects of worship but was undoubtedly thinking about the implications of them. In fact, in some languages it may be necessary to specify the elements of seeing and thinking by translating ‘for as I walked around and saw your objects of worship and thought about them.’

s.d: to continue to think back upon

s.c: In a number of languages adoption is spoken of as ‘making a child a son’ or ‘causing a child to become a daughter.’ In some instances the equivalent expression is merely ‘to treat someone as a son’ or ‘… daughter.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Eat, Drink
s.d: to eat a meal, with possible reference to the fact of the people reclining to eat{N:001}
s.g: to eat a meal
s.c: In biblical times there were apparently three different positions involved in the eating of a meal. People might, for example, (1) be seated on cushions around a low table or (2) be seated on chairs around a table or (3) recline on couches facing a table. Meals which involved reclining on couches would normally have been more elaborate, but the verbs ἀνάκειμαι and κατάκειμαι have been generalized in meaning to denote the eating of a meal without necessarily specifying the particular reclining position of those who participated in the meal.|For the translator, it may be extremely awkward to speak of ‘reclining to eat,’ since this may have connotations of people who are too lazy to sit up at the table or who are too sick to partake of an ordinary meal. It is for that reason that instead of rendering ἀνάκειμαι or κατάκειμαι as ‘to recline to eat,’ translators use expressions such as ‘to sit down to eat’ or ‘to eat a meal.’

s.dp: Stances and Events Related to Stances › Recline [to eat]
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to recline on the bosom) to take the place of honor at a meal
s.g: to dine in the place of honor
s.c: These expressions in ⟦John 13:23|John 13:23⟧ and ⟦John 13:25|John 13:25⟧ would mean that the so-called ‘beloved disciple’ would be at the right of Jesus, since guests at a meal would be reclining on the left side so as to permit freedom of the right hand in dining. It may, of course, be that the same expression could be used of persons sitting at a table rather than reclining on couches.|Literal translations of ἀνάκειμαι ἐν τῷ κόλπῳ and ἀναπίπτω ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος can result in serious misunderstanding, since they might imply overt homosexuality. There is no justification for reading into such idioms this type of implication.

s.c: In some languages it may be difficult to speak of ‘causing someone to become refreshed by resting.’ Normally this would be accomplished simply by causing a person not to have to work. Accordingly, ⟦Matthew 11:28|Matthew 11:28⟧ may be expressed in some languages as ‘I will make it possible for you no longer to have to work’ or ‘… to toil hard.’ This, however, must not be understood merely in the sense of ‘to give a person a vacation’ or ‘to make it possible for someone to live without working.’

s.d: to become physically refreshed after ceasing activity or work
s.g: rest; to rest
s.c: In the use of ἀναπαύομαι and ἀνάπαυσις, the focus of meaning seems to be upon the restorative character of rest rather than mere cessation of activity (see LN 68.34).

s.d: to remain in a place, with the implication of continuing to rest
s.g: to remain; to abide

s.d: to continue to be in a state in or on someone, with the implication of beneficent result
s.g: to remain on; to continue to be on

s.d: to persuade, with the possible implication of resistance and/or for wrong motives or results
s.g: to persuade; to incite

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: pertaining to a state of being maimed or mutilated, resulting in a crippling condition
s.g: maimed; mutilated; crippled

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to send back to a previous location
s.g: to send back

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to send on or up to some higher or appropriate authority
s.g: to send on; to send up

s.dp: Stances and Events Related to Stances › Recline [to eat]
s.d: to be in a reclining position as one eats (with the focus either upon the position or the act of eating)
s.g: to recline; to eat; to be at table; to eat; to dine; to sit down to eat

s.dp: Stances and Events Related to Stances › Recline [to eat]
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to recline on the bosom) to take the place of honor at a meal
s.g: to dine in the place of honor
s.c: These expressions in ⟦John 13:23|John 13:23⟧ and ⟦John 13:25|John 13:25⟧ would mean that the so-called beloved disciple would be at the right of Jesus, since guests at a meal would be reclining on the left side so as to permit freedom of the right hand in dining. It may, of course, be that the same expression could be used of persons sitting at a table rather than reclining on couches.|Literal translations of ἀνάκειμαι ἐν τῷ κόλπῳ and ἀναπίπτω ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος can result in serious misunderstanding, since they might imply overt homosexuality. There is no justification for reading into such idioms this type of implication.|This expression (ἀναπεσὼν … ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος) in ⟦John 13:25|John 13:25⟧ (following on ἀνακείμενος … ἐν τῷ κόλπῳ in ⟦John 13:23|John 13:23⟧) seems to be typical of the tendency of the Gospel of John to employ relatively close synonyms with essentially the same meaning. It is possible, however, in view of the aorist participle in ⟦John 13:25|John 13:25⟧ that the phrase ἀναπεσὼν ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος could also be understood in a more literal sense to mean ‘to move closer to the side (of Jesus).’

s.d: to make something total or complete
s.g: to make complete; to complete the number of
s.c: For another interpretation of ἀναπληρόω in ⟦1 Thessalonians 2:16|1 Thessalonians 2:16⟧, see LN 68.27.

s.d: to provide what has been lacking
s.g: to provide what is lacking; to make up for

s.d: to cause to happen, with the implication of fulfilling some purpose{N:001}
s.g: to cause to happen; to make happen; to fulfill

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to occupy a designated place
s.g: to occupy; to be in
s.c: It is possible, however, to understand ἀναπληρόω in ⟦1 Corinthians 14:16|1 Corinthians 14:16⟧ as specifically referring to fulfilling a particular function. One could therefore translate this phrase in ⟦1 Corinthians 14:16|1 Corinthians 14:16⟧ as ‘one who takes part in the service as an ordinary person.’

s.d: to conform to some standard as a means of demonstrating its purpose
s.g: to obey; to conform to; to submit to

s.d: to bring something to completion, with emphasis upon the process
s.g: to bring to completion; to cause to be complete
s.c: For another interpretation of ἀναπληρόω in ⟦1 Thessalonians 2:16|1 Thessalonians 2:16⟧, see LN 59.33.

s.d: pertaining to not being able to defend oneself or to justify one’s actions
s.g: to be without excuse; to have no excuse

s.d: to cause something to be unrolled
s.g: to unroll a scroll; to unroll (a book in the form of) a scroll

s.d: to cause the process of burning to begin
s.g: to ignite; to kindle; to set ablaze; to start a fire; to light a lamp
s.c: As already noted in the series of terms listed in LN 14.63, languages differ appreciably in terms employed for different phases and results of burning. For example, to set something on fire for the sake of providing warmth may be expressed by quite a different term from that which is used in speaking of the process of setting something on fire in order to destroy it.|It is possible that ἀνάπτω differs from ἅπτω either in the intensity of the activity or with special emphasis upon the initial phase of setting something on fire.

s.d: pertaining to what cannot be counted
s.g: countless; innumerable; beyond counting
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘countless’ is ‘so many that no one can count’ or ‘so many that there are no numbers left.’

s.d: to cause people to riot against
s.g: to stir up against; to start a riot; to cause an uproar

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: to cause someone distress and worry
s.g: to distress; to upset

s.d: to pull or draw something in an upward direction
s.g: to pull up; to draw up
s.c: In a number of languages clear distinctions are made on the basis of the means by which something is pulled or drawn. For example, to pull something by means of a rope may be entirely different from a term indicating that the object itself has been seized and is being drawn or dragged.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to come back to life after having once died
s.g: to come back to life; to live again; to be resurrected; resurrection
s.c: In a number of languages there is a difficulty involved in formulating some expression for ‘resurrection’ or ‘living again,’ since such a phrase may refer to what is technically known as metempsychosis, that is to say, the rebirth of the soul in another existence, a belief which is widely held in a number of areas of south Asia. This problem may be avoided in some languages by speaking of ‘his body will live again’ or ‘his body will come back to life’ or ‘he will be the same person when he lives again.’|One may also translate ‘there is no resurrection’ as ‘people will not live again.’

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: a process of change from a lower to a higher status (note the contrast with {L:πτῶσις<SDBG:πτῶσις:000001>}[b] ‘a falling,’ {D:87.75})
s.g: to rise; to rise up; rising up
s.c: ἀνάστασις in ⟦Luke 2:34|Luke 2:34⟧ may also be interpreted merely as a change for the better (see LN 13.60).|Reversals of rank and status are a frequent theme in the declaration of the prophets, and this becomes particularly significant in the Magnificat (see ⟦Luke 1:46|Luke 1:46⟧).

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: a change for the better
s.g: rising up
s.c: For another interpretation of ἀνάστασις in ⟦Luke 2:34|Luke 2:34⟧, see LN 87.39.

s.d: to cause people to rebel against or to reject authority
s.g: to incite to revolt; to cause to rebel

s.d: to cause to die on a cross a second time
s.g: to crucify again
s.c: In extrabiblical Greek ἀνασταυρόω is essentially equivalent in meaning to σταυρόω (LN 20.76), but in ⟦Hebrews 6:6|Hebrews 6:6⟧ ἀνασταυρόω is used figuratively of believers whose sin causes Christ to be crucified again in the sense of exposing Christ to public shame by virtue of the misdeeds of his professed followers. Some scholars, however, interpret ἀνασταυρόω in ⟦Hebrews 6:6|Hebrews 6:6⟧ as referring simply to the original crucifixion and thus interpret ἀνασταυρόω as being essentially synonymous with σταυρόω.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Laugh, Cry, Groan
s.d: to groan or to sigh deeply or intensely
s.g: to groan deeply; to sigh deeply

s.d: to move back to a point or area from which one has previously departed, but with more explicit emphasis upon the return (compare {L:ὑποστρέφω<SDBG:ὑποστρέφω:000000>}[a], {D:15.88})
s.g: to move back; to return

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Behavior, Conduct
s.d: to conduct oneself, with apparent focus upon overt daily behavior{N:001}
s.g: to live; to conduct oneself; to behave; behavior; conduct

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Behavior, Conduct
s.d: to conduct oneself, with apparent focus upon overt daily behavior{N:001}
s.g: to live; to conduct oneself; to behave; behavior; conduct

s.dp: Arrange, Organize › Organize [of events and states]
s.d: to organize a series of items
s.g: to organize (a report); to arrange; to compile; to put together

s.d: to move up, especially of the upward movement of the sun, stars, or clouds
s.g: to come up; to move upward; to rise

s.d: to change from darkness to light in the early morning hours
s.g: to dawn; to become light
s.c: In some languages dawning is divided into more than one aspect or period of time. The first may be only a glimmering of light in the east; the second period makes visibility quite easy; and the third period involves shafts of light or colored clouds visible in the sky immediately before sunrise. Usually an expression for one of these periods of time is more generalized in usage, and therefore it is probably satisfactory to adopt such an expression for any transition from darkness to light.

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἀνατέλλω<SDBG:ἀνατέλλω:000000>}[a] ‘to rise,’ as of the sun, {D:15.104}) to be an important descendant, presumably of a distinguished ancestor, normally with a number of intervening generations
s.g: be a descendant; offspring

s.d: to explain something, presumably by putting forward additional or different information
s.g: to explain; to make clear

s.d: to move up, especially of the upward movement of the sun, stars, or clouds
s.g: to come up; to move upward; to rise
s.c: It is also possible to understand ἀνατολή in ⟦Matthew 2:2|Matthew 2:2⟧ as meaning ‘the east’ (see ἀνατολή, LN 82.1).

s.dp: Spacial Orientations › North, South, East, West
s.d: east (as the direction of the rising sun)
s.g: east
s.c: In most languages east and west are related to the rising or setting sun, although in some languages there may be some local geographical feature which serves as a marker of direction, for example, the location of a particular mountain, the ocean, or a river. For north, some languages employ ‘to the left of the rising sun,’ that is to say, the direction is oriented in terms of the left hand of a person facing toward the rising sun. Similarly, south would be ‘to the right of the rising sun.’

s.d: (an idiom, literally: dawning from on high) the bright dawn of salvation (or possibly to be understood as a title for the Messiah)
s.g: the dawn from on high
s.c: The expression ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψους occurs in a highly poetic liturgical passage in Luke 1, and many translators have preferred to retain the more or less literal rendering. Others, however, have interpreted this as the dawning of salvation and have therefore translated ἐπισκέψεται ἡμᾶς ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψους as ‘salvation will dawn upon us from heaven’ or ‘from heaven salvation will come to us as the dawn does.’ If one wishes to employ ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψους as simply a title for the Messiah, one can translate ‘the Messiah will come to us,’ but it is normally better to preserve the figurative expression and relate it to the coming of the Messiah as ‘the Messiah will come to us even as the dawn does from on high.’ One may also treat the problem of interpretation in a footnote.

s.d: to cause something to be completely overturned
s.g: to turn over; to upset; to overturn

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἀνατρέπω<SDBG:ἀνατρέπω:000000>}[a] ‘to overturn,’ {D:16.18}) to cause serious difficulty or trouble with regard to someone’s belief
s.g: to upset belief

s.dp: Help, Care For › Rear, Bring Up
s.d: to raise a child to maturity by providing for physical and psychological needs{N:001}
s.g: to raise; to rear; to bring up
s.c: To raise or bring up children may be expressed in a number of different ways, for example, ‘to give food to children,’ ‘to take care of children,’ ‘to be a parent to children,’ ‘to cause a child to become an adult,’ or ‘to make a child become like oneself.’

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to be trained at the feet of) to be given extensive and formal instruction by someone
s.g: to be taught by; to be educated under the direction of
s.c: In a number of languages the closest equivalent of this part of ⟦Acts 22:3|Acts 22:3⟧ is simply ‘Gamaliel was his teacher.’

s.d: to come to a point of being visible, with focus upon the process of becoming seen
s.g: to come to be seen; to appear; to come into view
s.c: In a number of languages there may be difficulties involved in speaking of ‘the kingdom of God appearing.’ It may not be difficult to speak of a ‘person appearing,’ because an individual may ‘show himself’ or ‘cause himself to be seen.’ It may therefore be necessary to render this expression in ⟦Luke 19:11|Luke 19:11⟧ as ‘that soon people will be seeing the kingdom of God’ or ‘… experiencing the kingdom of God’ or ‘… become aware of the kingdom of God.’

s.d: to bring or lead up
s.g: to bring up; to lead up

s.d: to be carried or borne upward
s.g: to carry up

s.d: to offer up someone or something as a sacrifice (a technical term in the sacrificial system)
s.g: to offer; to offer up; to make an offering
